cos: Distribution + UX; monetises via P2M devices, lending & insurance cross-sell

Runs on NPCI's UPI switch, accessed through sponsor PSP banks (Yes Bank, ICICI) — every UPI app must ride on a bank's licence, which is why 'TPAP' means third-party. Unusually, PhonePe hosts on its own data centres rather than public cloud, and has built its fraud-detection engine in-house on its transaction telemetry.

Connects to UPI through PSP handles at four partner banks (Axis, HDFC, SBI, ICICI), giving it redundancy if any one bank's systems slow down. The app runs on Google's global infrastructure, with India payments data localised to comply with RBI's data-residency circular.

After RBI shut down its in-house Paytm Payments Bank in 2024, Paytm migrated its UPI handles to four partner PSP banks (Axis, Yes, SBI, HDFC) — a case study in regulatory dependency. It retains its own Payment Aggregator licence from RBI for the merchant-acquiring side.
Affluent-user niche; credit-card bill payment wedge

Rides Axis Bank's PSP infrastructure for UPI access. Its real asset is data-driven gating: users are admitted based on credit scores pulled from bureaus (TransUnion CIBIL), giving CRED a pre-filtered affluent audience it monetises through lending and commerce.
Challengers gaining share ahead of the 30%-cap deadline

All ride partner PSP banks for UPI access — none needs its own licence. super.money leans on Flipkart's checkout traffic for distribution; BHIM is owned and run by NPCI itself. Their combined rise (≈6.5%) is partly strategic positioning for the market-share cap that bites 31 Dec 2026.

cos: One-stop merchant acceptance + business banking + capital

Acquires card payments through partner acquiring banks (Axis, RBL, ICICI) running on Visa/Mastercard rails, and UPI through sponsor banks on NPCI rails. Merchant onboarding KYC is automated using government identity APIs — Aadhaar (from UIDAI), PAN validation (NSDL e-Gov) and the central KYC registry (CERSAI). Infrastructure runs on AWS's Indian regions.

Processes cards through bank acquirers on the international card networks. Its LazyPay pay-later product underwrites using credit-bureau records combined with PayU's own checkout behaviour data — an example of a gateway converting payment flow into lending signal.

POS terminals connect to both NPCI rails (RuPay, UPI) and Visa/Mastercard. Its brand-EMI engine plugs directly into issuer banks' loan systems so a phone buyer gets an instant EMI at the till — the brand, bank and Pine Labs share the subvention. Gift cards run on its own Qwikcilver rails.

Its payouts product (the strength) pushes money out over IMPS and UPI rails through partner banks — used for refunds, vendor payments, gig wages. Its verification suite repackages government data sources (Aadhaar, PAN, bank-account penny-drop, GSTIN) into single developer APIs.

Built on UPI QR interoperability — an NPCI standard that means one printed QR accepts payments from every app, which is what let BharatPe give QRs away free. Monetisation comes from merchant loans funded by NBFC partners, with BharatPe earning origination and collection fees.

zones.prof: mixed; Juspay profitable, issuing platforms still investing
cos: Its SDK sits inside merchant apps (Amazon, Swiggy scale) and routes each transaction to whichever gateway or bank has the best success rate at that moment. Consumes NPCI's UPI specifications and the card networks' tokenisation APIs (Visa VTS, Mastercard MDES). Currently piloting agentic payments with NPCI and OpenAI.
Issuing & credit APIs for fintechs and banks

A fintech that wants to launch a card programme gets its BIN (card-number range) sponsored by an M2P partner bank, with M2P running the technology stack on Visa or RuPay rails — the fintech never touches the card network directly.
Modern core-banking + issuing stack for banks
Sells cloud-native processing to banks themselves (e.g., HDFC Bank's PayZapp rebuild) — modernising the incumbents from within rather than riding on top of them.

Packages India's public infrastructure into developer-friendly APIs: Bharat Connect bill payments (an NPCI system), Account Aggregator data flows (RBI framework, governed through the Sahamati alliance) and UPI deep links.
Their licensed switch software runs inside the PSP banks and processes the actual UPI messages — the invisible layer between the app you tap and NPCI's central switch.
Owns & operates UPI, IMPS, RuPay, NETC, AePS, Bharat Connect; writes the scheme rules

A not-for-profit promoted by RBI and the Indian Banks' Association — effectively a public utility. It runs the central switches, earns small per-transaction switching fees, and publishes the rulebook (circulars on caps, interchange, API limits) that every player in zones 1–3 must code against.
Own the global card networks, plus the tokenisation infrastructure (VTS/MDES) that every Indian gateway now consumes — mandatory since RBI banned merchants from storing raw card numbers in 2022.

Licenses the UPI stack to other countries (UAE, Namibia, Peru), builds bilateral links like UPI–PayNow with Singapore, and connects to BIS Project Nexus — the multilateral effort to link national instant-payment systems.

cos: Largest PSP handle base — PhonePe's primary sponsor

Every @ybl UPI address resolves through Yes Bank's systems. The bank holds NPCI membership and RBI settlement accounts on behalf of the TPAPs it sponsors, earning float income and processing fees — licence-as-a-service, essentially.
Play every banking role in the chain simultaneously

PSP sponsors for the consumer apps, acquiring banks for the gateways, and settlement banks for merchant payouts. Their UPI switches typically run FSS or Mindgate software layered over Finacle (Infosys) or Flexcube (Oracle) core-banking systems.

Provide BIN sponsorship for card programmes and the escrow/nodal accounts that RBI's Payment Aggregator rules require every gateway to maintain — small banks that turned fintech partnership into a business line.
Automated merchant & user onboarding (video-KYC, document AI)

Orchestrate government identity infrastructure into onboarding flows: Aadhaar eKYC and offline XML from UIDAI, the central KYC registry run by CERSAI, DigiLocker documents from MeitY, and PAN checks via NSDL e-Gov. On top they add their own computer vision for liveness detection and document-forgery checks.
Device intelligence & fraud scoring at onboarding

Scores risk from device fingerprints and behavioural signals (SIM age, typing cadence, network graph), enriched by telco data partnerships — designed to catch mule accounts and synthetic identities before KYC even begins.

The large gateways and apps run their own real-time fraud engines using velocity rules and tokenised network data on their proprietary traffic — scale of data is the moat, which is why the biggest players build rather than buy.
Licenses and supervises the whole chain

Statutory authority under the Payment & Settlement Systems Act, 2007. Licenses Payment Aggregators and wallet issuers, sets PSP and KYC rules, and itself operates the wholesale rails (RTGS/NEFT) that final settlement runs on.

Issues the circulars that move markets: the 30% TPAP market-share cap, interchange on PPI-UPI transactions, API rate limits. Not a statutory regulator, but in practice every product roadmap in zones 1–3 is written around NPCI circulars.

Since merchants pay no fee on UPI, the economics are propped up by a government incentive scheme (≈₹1,500–3,500 cr/yr from the union budget) paid to banks for small-ticket merchant transactions — the single most debated policy issue in Indian payments.

Volunteer think-tank that authored the India Stack, OCEN and DEPA specifications which NPCI and RBI later institutionalised. Sahamati now governs the Account Aggregator ecosystem as an industry alliance.
Cloud hosting for most gateways and apps

Host the bulk of Indian payments workloads in India-region data centres, because RBI's 2018 data-localisation circular requires payments data to be stored only in India. Regulated-workload compliance is a selling point of their Mumbai/Hyderabad regions.
License the switching software banks run to connect to card networks and NPCI, often bundled with managed services — decades-old plumbing that most fintech demos quietly depend on.

Every UPI registration depends on an outbound SMS for device binding, and OTPs ride TRAI-regulated SMS routes. Telco outages are an under-appreciated single point of failure for the entire consumer payments stack.

Contract manufacturers (Indian and Chinese) build the payment-confirmation soundboxes and POS devices for Paytm, PhonePe and GPay — hardware subscription revenue is now a key monetisation lever in zone 1.
